bai.moTa: Narrow the position packet and watch its momentum distribution broaden.
bai.yChinh: Position and momentum describe the same state. For a Gaussian without quadratic phase, the product of standard deviations reaches its minimum.
bai.giaiThich: The two curves are normalized densities with separate axes. Blue uses nm for position and gold uses ℏ/nm for momentum. The dots sample two ensembles of identically prepared particles.
bai.conSo.1: At σx = 1 nm, the minimum packet has σp = 0.5 ℏ/nm.
bai.conSo.2: An electron with σx = 1 nm has a velocity standard deviation of about 58 km/s; after about 30 fs of free flight the packet is twice as wide.
bai.hieuDung: Uncertainty is the intrinsic spread of outcomes for one preparation. A particular instrument may add measurement error.
bai.nguon: Prepared by Trí Lữ. OpenStax, University Physics, Vol. 3, `7.2; D. J. Griffiths and D. F. Schroeter, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, Chs. 1 and 2.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.1: Read mean and standard deviation on each axis.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.2: Predict the effects of shifts and width changes.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.3: Prepare a packet whose uncertainty product is larger than the bound ℏ/2 while the position density stays the same.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.4: Explain why a free packet spreads over time while its momentum width stays fixed.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.1.noiDung:
Prepare many copies of one state. Measure position on one ensemble and momentum on another. Each dot is one outcome; rate-limited clicks illustrate detections.

Use the same source and different detectors in separate trials. Two dots aligned in the drawing are not paired outcomes for a single particle. Inspect the thickness of each entire band around its center and compare it with the spacing of its markers.

$$ \int \rho_x(x)\,dx=\int \rho_p(p)\,dp=1 $$

+++ A closer look · Separate axes
Each area is one. Heights use different units, so read widths on their respective axes.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Resample both ensembles|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.2.noiDung:
Markers on either side of the mean are one standard deviation from it. A single outcome can fall outside them.

Suppose you measure the distance between the leftmost and rightmost dots. It can grow during a long run as rare distant outcomes appear. The standard deviation uses the full distribution and better characterizes the preparation than those two extreme observations.

$$ \sigma_x^2=\langle(x-\langle x\rangle)^2\rangle $$

+++ A closer look · Why square deviations?
Left and right deviations cancel in an average. Squaring retains the size of deviations on both sides.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Set σx = 1 nm|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.noiDung:
A narrow packet requires a broader superposition of wave numbers. Momentum is proportional to wave number, so momentum spread increases.

Move the right position marker closer to its mean. Blue must rise because the same probability is more concentrated. If you expect gold to narrow too, compare its marker spacing before and after dragging. Identify which observable now has more predictable outcomes.

$$ p=\hbar k $$

+++ A closer look · Minimum packet
With zero quadratic phase, halving σx doubles σp. The blue peak rises to preserve area.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Compare with the initial packet|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.thuThach.de: Drag the blue handle to σp = 1 ℏ/nm within 0.05 ℏ/nm.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.thuThach.goiY: At zero quadratic phase, try σx near 0.5 nm.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.noiDung:
Moving the entire state to the right shifts its position mean. The momentum distribution retains its shape and center.

Check this in two readings. Record the momentum width, shift the position mean right, then read the same quantity. New dots are sampled and need not match the old ones. Compare the distribution shape and its width readout.

$$ \psi(x)\longrightarrow\psi(x-x_0) $$

+++ A closer look · Phase in the spectrum
Translation multiplies the momentum amplitude by a phase factor. Its squared magnitude removes that phase.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Shift center to 1 nm|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.noiDung:
Multiplying by a linear phase shifts the momentum spectrum sideways. Position width stays fixed. Both distributions come from the same state.

The yellow handle sits at the centre of the momentum spectrum. Dragging it shifts the whole yellow curve sideways: the peak moves, and the two yellow marks follow it without spreading apart. The blue curve does not change at all, because the position density cannot see a linear phase. That phase still has a real effect: the packet gains an average velocity p₀/m and will drift once time runs in Step 9.

$$ \psi(x)\longrightarrow e^{ip_0x/\hbar}\psi(x) $$

+++ A closer look · Center versus spread
A larger mean momentum need not give a larger momentum uncertainty. The uncertainty measures spread around the new mean.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Reset momentum mean to 0|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.thuThach.de: Drag the gold mean to +1 ℏ/nm at σx = 1 nm. Momentum tolerance is 0.08 ℏ/nm.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.thuThach.goiY: The gold handle moves the center of the lower spectrum.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.noiDung:
Every state obeys the position–momentum inequality. A Gaussian with linear phase can reach equality. Changing its width trades one spread for the other.

Prepare two packets at very different positions and give them the same width. At zero C the readouts give identical products. Distinguish ignorance of the chosen mean from a known mean with outcomes still dispersed over repetitions.

$$ \sigma_x\sigma_p\geq\hbar/2 $$

+++ A closer look · Origin of the bound
Position and momentum do not commute. Their commutator sets this bound on standard deviations for normalized states with finite variances.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Choose a broad packet|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.noiDung:
Set the quadratic phase coefficient C away from zero. Phase changes more rapidly far from the center. Position density stays Gaussian and unchanged while momentum spread grows.

This produces physically different states with identical position-density snapshots. Record the gold-marker spacing before changing C. As its magnitude grows, momentum broadens while blue stays fixed. Phase contains information absent from the position image.

$$ \sigma_x\sigma_p=\frac{\hbar}{2}\sqrt{1+C^2} $$

+++ A closer look · Definition of C
The extra phase factor is $e^{iC(x-x_0)^2/(4\sigma_x^2)}$. Both signs of C give the same uncertainty product, but positive C describes a packet that is spreading and negative C one that is focusing (see Step 9).
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Try C = 1|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.noiDung:
Changing width and adding phase are distinct operations. Position density alone can hide phase; momentum measurements distinguish states with identical position densities.

Return to a minimum packet, choose a position width, and note both widths. Keep blue fixed and vary C. If only one width grows, the principle is still satisfied: the inequality sets a lower bound; states need not all attain it.

$$ \sigma_p=\frac{\hbar}{2\sigma_x}\sqrt{1+C^2} $$

+++ A closer look · Preparation matters
C belongs to the state’s phase. Set C to zero to recover a minimum packet and drag the width to test the bound.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Set C to 0|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.thuThach.de: Set C to 0, then drag the blue handle to σx = 1.5 nm within 0.06 nm.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.thuThach.goiY: Read σx on the width control and the product on the readout.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.9.ten: A free packet spreads over time
bai.baiGiang.buoc.9.noiDung:
Release the minimum packet and let the electron fly freely, with no force acting on it. The yellow curve stays put: with no force, the momentum of every component is unchanged, so σp stays the same. The blue curve widens and sinks.

The reason lies in the momentum width itself. The packet contains both fast and slow components, whose velocities differ by about $\sigma_v=\sigma_p/m$. After a time t they have drifted apart by an extra $\sigma_v t$ or so. Meanwhile a quadratic phase builds up by itself: C grows from 0, so the product σxσp rises above ℏ/2, just as in Step 7.

$$ \sigma_x(t)=\sigma_x\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\hbar t}{2m\sigma_x^2}\right)^2} $$

> [Ví dụ] An electron with σx = 1 nm has σv of about 58 km/s. After about 17 fs the packet is $\sqrt2$ nm wide, after about 30 fs it is 2 nm wide. A narrower 0.5 nm packet spreads four times faster: its characteristic time is only about 4.3 fs.

> [Hiểu sai thường gặp] The packet does not spread because the electron gets «smeared» or because the detector gets worse. The momentum distribution was there from the moment of preparation; time merely turns the spread in momentum into a spread in position.

+++ Đi sâu · Negative C: the packet focuses before it spreads
When C is positive, the components at the edges move outward: the packet is already spreading. When C is negative, the edges move toward the centre: the packet narrows down to exactly the bound ℏ/2 and only then spreads. In general $\sigma_x^2(t)=\sigma_x^2+(\hbar/m)Ct+(\sigma_p t/m)^2$, and the new phase coefficient is $C(t)=C+2(\sigma_p/\hbar)^2(\hbar/m)t$. The lesson's numerical test recomputes both with a numerical Fourier transform.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Release the packet|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.9.thuThach.de: Keep σx = 1 nm and C = 0 at the start, then drag the time until σx(t) = 2 nm, within 0.05 nm.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.9.thuThach.goiY: The width doubles when ℏt/(2mσx²) equals the square root of three, about 30 fs.
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.1.y: C is the quadratic phase coefficient.
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.4.y: Minimum packet at t = 0; σp does not change with time.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.hoi: Halve σx of a minimum packet. What happens to σp?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.hoi: How does translating the position mean change momentum width?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.giai: The spectrum acquires only a phase.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.hoi: How does reversing C change the product?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.giai: The product depends on C squared.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.hoi: A minimum electron packet 1 nm wide flies freely for about 30 fs. What is true?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.giai: With no force the momentum distribution stays the same. Fast and slow components drift apart, so σx grows and the product exceeds ℏ/2. Choosing «σp halves» assumes the product always equals ℏ/2.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.dap: So each distribution is measured on the same initial preparation.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.6.hoi: Does equality hold for every state?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.6.dap: Only special states reach the minimum. Nonzero C increases the product here.
